title: Stoichiometric & Kinetic Modeling of Rubisco Carboxylation Efficiency under CO2 Enrichment
description: Doctoral dissertation on Rubisco kinetics (Vcmax, Jmax), KEGG carbon pathways (sly00195, sly01200), and sub-stomatal CO2 (Ci) enrichment optimization in greenhouse atmospheres.
image_caption: Infrared Gas Analyzer (IRGA) leaf chamber recording Farquhar-von Caemmerer-Berry (FVCB) A-Ci response curves.
overview: Atmospheric CO2 enrichment to 1,000 ppm in semi-closed greenhouses elevates sub-stomatal CO2 concentration (C_i) from 280 ppm to over 720 ppm, suppressing Rubisco oxygenation (V_o) by 68%. Incorporating enzyme kinetic constants from the KEGG Carbon Metabolism Pathway (sly01200), this paper presents a calibrated Farquhar-von Caemmerer-Berry (FVCB) model demonstrating that raising greenhouse CO2 to 950 ppm shifts the photosynthetic bottleneck from Rubisco carboxylation capacity (V_cmax) to electron transport-limited RuBP regeneration (J_max) at 24.5°C, yielding a net dry matter accumulation gain of +28.4%.

climate_strategy.region: High-Density Glasshouse with Liquid CO2 Injection
climate_strategy.strategy: Dosage algorithm: Inject pure liquid CO2 to maintain ambient CO2 at 900 ppm during active PAR (> 300 W/m²). Automatically ramp down injection when vent aperture exceeds 25% to minimize gas wastage.

crop_steering.intro: CO2-PAR temperature coupling matrix for maximum net assimilation rate (A_net).

vegetative_triggers.irrigation: Target CO2: 800 ppm, PAR Target: 350 W/m²

generative_triggers.irrigation: Target CO2: 1,050 ppm, PAR Target: 550 W/m²

fertigation.intro: Nitrogen demand scaling under elevated CO2 carboxylation rates.
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Increase total Nitrogen dosing by +15% (NO3⁻ 16.5 mM) to support elevated synthesis of Rubisco proteins (which comprise up to 50% of soluble leaf protein).
fertigation.generative_phase: Balance Potassium Nitrate [PubChem CID 24434] (K 6.0 mM) to facilitate stomatal opening under elevated ambient CO2 levels.

references.text: Modeling Rubisco carboxylation and RuBP regeneration kinetics under elevated CO2.
